name: Chocolate brownies
tip: A rich chocolate bake with a crackly top and fudgy centre; cool before cutting for neat squares.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 20 cm square tin with parchment.
Melt the butter with dark chocolate gently; cool for a few minutes.
Whisk sugar and eggs together for 2 minutes, then stir in the melted chocolate.
Fold in flour and cocoa powder, then chocolate chips; avoid overmixing.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the top is set but the centre still has a slight wobble.
Cool fully in the tin before slicing into nine squares. Store chilled if adding a dairy topping.

name: Sticky toffee pudding
tip: Soft date sponge with warm toffee sauce; delicious with vanilla ice cream. Preparation and baking take around 55 minutes.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a six-portion muffin tin or a small 20 cm baking dish.
Cover the chopped dates with 180 ml boiling water, leave 10 minutes, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda and mash until soft.
Cream 75 g of butter with 100 g of brown sugar; beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour and date mixture.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes, or until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
For the sauce, gently simmer the remaining 35 g butter, 60 g brown sugar, cream and golden syrup for 3–5 minutes until glossy.
Serve the warm sponge with toffee sauce and ice cream. Refrigerate any dairy leftovers promptly.

name: Lemon drizzle cake
tip: A buttery lemon sponge soaked with citrus syrup and finished with a simple glaze.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Beat softened butter with 160 g caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Add eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, baking powder and finely grated zest of two lemons; loosen with the milk.
Bake for 45–50 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Warm the juice of two lemons with the remaining 40 g caster sugar; prick the warm loaf and pour over.
When cool, mix icing sugar with enough juice from the third lemon to make a thick drizzle and spoon over the cake.

name: Classic apple crumble
tip: A crunchy oat topping over soft cinnamon apples. Add custard just before serving.
method: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Peel, core and slice the apples.
Toss apples with 40 g sugar and cinnamon in a medium baking dish; add 2 tbsp water.
Rub flour and cold cubed butter together with fingertips until breadcrumb-like, then stir in oats and remaining 90 g sugar.
Scatter the crumble over the fruit without pressing it down.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling at the edges.
Allow 5 minutes to settle; warm the custard separately and serve alongside.

name: Eton mess
tip: A quick, no-bake combination of sweet strawberries, whipped cream and crisp meringue.
method: Wash and dry the strawberries; slice three-quarters and crush the rest lightly with icing sugar to make a quick sauce.
Whip cold double cream with vanilla to soft peaks; do not overwhip.
Break the meringue nests into bite-sized pieces.
Layer or gently fold together the cream, sliced berries, crushed berries and meringue.
Spoon into four glasses and serve immediately so the meringue stays crisp.

name: Victoria sponge cake
tip: Classic two-layer sponge with strawberry jam and softly whipped cream; chill after filling.
method: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan); grease and line two 20 cm sandwich tins.
Beat softened butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy; add eggs one at a time, then vanilla.
Fold in flour and baking powder gently; divide mixture evenly between the tins.
Bake for 22–27 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean; cool completely on a rack.
Whip the cold cream to soft peaks; spread jam on one sponge and cream over it, then sandwich together.
Dust with icing sugar and keep chilled because of the fresh cream; serve promptly.

name: Bread and butter pudding
tip: An old-fashioned baked custard pudding with lightly spiced bread and raisins.
method: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and butter a medium baking dish.
Spread butter on the bread slices, cut each into triangles and layer with raisins in the dish.
Whisk eggs, milk, cream, sugar, vanilla and cinnamon together.
Pour custard over bread, pressing lightly so every slice absorbs it; leave to soak for 15 minutes.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until golden, puffed and just set in the centre.
Rest 10 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.

name: Chocolate mousse
tip: An egg-free, airy chocolate mousse; allow at least two hours in the fridge to set.
method: Break chocolate into small pieces and melt gently over a pan of barely simmering water; let it cool until just warm.
Whip 300 ml of the cold cream with icing sugar and vanilla to soft peaks, not stiff peaks.
Mix a spoonful of whipped cream into the melted chocolate to loosen it, then gently fold in the rest.
Divide between four glasses and chill for at least two hours until set.
Whip the remaining cream lightly and spoon on top of each mousse.
Serve with raspberries; keep refrigerated and eat within two days.

name: Banoffee pie
tip: Crunchy biscuit base, caramel, banana and whipped cream; chill the crust before assembly.
method: Crush biscuits finely and combine with melted butter.
Press into a 20–23 cm tart tin, covering the base and sides; refrigerate for at least one hour.
Spread the caramel evenly into the firm biscuit shell.
Slice the bananas and arrange them across the caramel.
Whip the cream with vanilla and icing sugar to soft peaks; pile over the bananas.
Grate chocolate over the top and chill until ready to serve; keep covered in the refrigerator.

name: No-bake raspberry cheesecake
tip: Creamy chilled cheesecake with a biscuit base and fresh berries. Allow at least four hours for chilling.
method: Line the base of a 20 cm springform cake tin with parchment.
Crush the biscuits, mix with melted butter and press firmly into the tin; chill while making the filling.
Beat cream cheese with icing sugar and vanilla until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip cold double cream to soft peaks; gently fold it into the cheese mixture.
Spoon over the chilled biscuit base, smooth the top and refrigerate for at least four hours, preferably overnight.
Remove from the tin and top with washed, dried berries just before serving. Keep refrigerated.

name: Chocolate chip cookies
tip: Soft-centred golden cookies with chocolate chunks; cook in batches if your tray is small.
method: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line two baking trays with parchment.
Beat softened butter with both sugars until creamy, then mix in the egg and vanilla.
Combine flour and bicarbonate of soda, then fold into the butter mixture with chocolate chips.
Divide into twelve mounds with plenty of space between them; chill dough 10 minutes if very soft.
Bake for 10–13 minutes until edges are golden and centres still look slightly soft.
Leave on the baking trays for 5 minutes before moving to a rack; cool before storing in an airtight tin.

name: Rice pudding
tip: Slow-simmered pudding rice with vanilla and cinnamon. Stir regularly to prevent sticking.
method: Put the pudding rice, milk and cream into a large heavy-based saucepan.
Add sugar, vanilla and half the cinnamon; bring just to a gentle simmer, stirring.
Cook uncovered on low heat for 40–45 minutes, stirring every few minutes so the rice does not catch.
Add a splash of milk if it becomes too thick before the rice is tender.
Stir in butter and spoon into bowls; dust with the remaining cinnamon and serve warm.
Cool leftovers rapidly, refrigerate within one hour, and eat within 24 hours; reheat until steaming hot only once.

name: Classic apple pie
tip: A golden pastry pie filled with tender cinnamon apples; cool slightly before slicing.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan); place a metal baking tray inside to heat.
Peel, core and thinly slice apples; toss with sugar, cinnamon, flour and lemon juice.
Roll two-thirds of the pastry to line a 23 cm pie dish, leaving a slight overhang; fill with apples.
Roll remaining pastry as a lid, seal and crimp the edges, cut two steam slits and brush with beaten egg.
Place pie dish on the hot baking tray; bake 20 minutes then lower oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and bake 25–35 minutes more until pastry is golden and apples are tender.
Rest 15–20 minutes before slicing; serve warm with ice cream.

name: No-churn chocolate ice cream
tip: Creamy homemade chocolate ice cream without a machine; allow six hours or overnight to freeze.
method: Melt the dark chocolate gently and leave to cool until just warm, not hot.
Mix condensed milk with cocoa powder, vanilla and cooled melted chocolate until smooth.
Whip cold double cream to soft peaks in a large bowl.
Fold the chocolate mixture through the whipped cream carefully until uniformly coloured.
Spoon into a freezer-safe lidded container, level the top and cover tightly.
Freeze at least six hours or overnight; soften at room temperature for 5–10 minutes before scooping.

name: Berry pavlova
tip: Crisp meringue shell, soft marshmallow centre and raspberry-topped cream. Cool meringue fully before filling.
method: Heat oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Draw a 20 cm circle on parchment and place pencil-side down on a tray.
Whisk egg whites in a clean, grease-free bowl until soft peaks form.
Add caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, whisking until very thick, glossy and no sugar grains are felt.
Fold in cornflour and vinegar, spoon into the circle and shape a shallow hollow in the centre.
Reduce oven to 120°C (100°C fan) and bake for 75 minutes. Turn oven off and leave the meringue inside to cool fully.
Whip cream with vanilla, spoon onto the cold pavlova and top with raspberries; serve soon after assembling.

name: Carrot cake
tip: Moist spiced carrot cake with cream-cheese icing; keep chilled after icing.
method: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan); line a 20 cm round cake tin with parchment.
Whisk oil, eggs and brown sugar, then fold in flour, cinnamon and mixed spice.
Grate carrots finely and fold them into the batter with chopped walnuts.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40–50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean; cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, softened butter and icing sugar into a smooth icing; avoid overbeating.
Spread icing on the cooled cake, sprinkle with extra walnuts if desired and refrigerate until serving.

name: Jam roly-poly
tip: Traditional rolled suet sponge with raspberry jam; bake wrapped in parchment and foil.
method: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and set a deep roasting tray of water on the lowest shelf.
Mix flour, suet and sugar, then stir in milk gradually to make a soft but not sticky dough.
Roll on a floured surface into a roughly 25 x 30 cm rectangle; spread jam, leaving a 2 cm border.
Roll up from a short edge, pinch the seam and ends closed, and wrap loosely in buttered baking parchment then foil to allow expansion.
Place the parcel seam-side down on a baking tray and bake for 45–55 minutes until the sponge is cooked through.
Unwrap carefully to avoid hot steam, cut into thick slices and serve with warm custard.

name: Tiramisu
tip: Coffee-soaked sponge with mascarpone cream. This version avoids raw eggs and alcohol; allow four hours to chill.
method: Brew strong coffee and let it cool completely.
Whisk mascarpone, icing sugar and vanilla until just smooth.
In another bowl whip the cold cream to soft peaks, then fold it gently into the mascarpone.
Dip each sponge finger briefly into the cold coffee and line the bottom of a 20 cm square dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over the sponge, then repeat with another coffee-dipped layer and remaining cream.
Cover and chill for at least four hours or overnight.
Dust with cocoa and grate dark chocolate over the top just before serving. Keep refrigerated.

name: Lemon cheesecake
tip: Zesty no-bake lemon cheesecake; refrigerate at least four hours before slicing.
method: Line the base of a 20 cm springform cake tin with baking parchment.
Crush biscuits to fine crumbs; mix with melted butter, press into the tin and chill for 20 minutes.
Beat cream cheese with icing sugar, vanilla and finely grated lemon zest until smooth.
Whisk cold cream to soft peaks, then gently fold into the cream-cheese mixture with 3–4 tbsp fresh lemon juice.
Spoon onto biscuit base, level and refrigerate at least four hours until firm.
Remove carefully from the tin and garnish with extra lemon zest; keep refrigerated until serving.

name: Chocolate profiteroles
tip: Crisp choux buns filled with whipped cream and finished with warm chocolate sauce.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two trays.
Bring 250 ml water and butter to the boil in a saucepan; immediately add all the flour and beat vigorously until the dough forms a ball.
Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs gradually until the paste is glossy and holds its shape.
Pipe or spoon 18 small mounds onto trays; bake 25–30 minutes until deep golden and dry. Do not open the oven early.
Pierce each bun to release steam, then cool completely on a rack.
Whip cold cream with icing sugar and vanilla; split the buns and fill just before serving.
Melt chocolate gently with milk and caster sugar, drizzle over the filled profiteroles and serve immediately.

name: Treacle tart
tip: A classic British golden-syrup tart, best served warm with cream or custard.
method: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin with pastry and trim the edges.
Prick the base, line with baking paper and baking beans, then blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans and bake for another 5 minutes.
Warm golden syrup gently to make it easier to pour; mix in breadcrumbs, lemon zest and juice, ground ginger and beaten egg.
Pour the mixture into the pastry shell and dot with the butter.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and set but still slightly soft in the middle.
Leave 15 minutes before slicing and serve with lightly whipped double cream.
